name: Midjourney
tagline: Text-to-image generation service known for high-quality aesthetic output

pricing.notes: Official docs checked 2026-07-30; Basic is $10/month, Standard $30, Pro $60, Mega $120.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 3.3 Fast GPU hours/month (about 200 minutes); 0 Relax GPU time

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 15 Fast GPU hours/month; unlimited Relax-mode image generations

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 30 Fast GPU hours/month; unlimited Relax-mode images and SD video; Stealth Mode

tiers.name: Mega
tiers.limits: 60 Fast GPU hours/month; unlimited Relax-mode images and SD video; Stealth Mode

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-20%), with annual plans paid upfront and auto-renewing
pricing.hiddenCosts: Unused monthly Fast GPU time does not roll over; extra Fast GPU time costs $4 per hour. Private/Stealth generation requires Pro or Mega. Companies with more than $1 million in annual gross revenue must use Pro or Mega.

verdictSummary: You can build a wrapper around open models, but you cannot solo-recreate Midjourney's proprietary model quality, style tuning, infrastructure, and community distribution.
coreLoopDIY: Use Stable Diffusion/Flux-style local or hosted models with a prompt UI and gallery.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay for the model and taste layer, not the chat box around it.

priorArt.name: ComfyUI
priorArt.desc: Open-source node-based UI for running image-generation workflows locally or on a GPU serve

alternatives.name: ComfyUI
alternatives.desc: Can produce superb images with current models, provided you are willing to become the workflow designer.

facts.install: Desktop app, Windows portable archive or Python source installation
facts.engines: Stable Diffusion, SDXL, SD3 and SD3.5, FLUX, Qwen Image, Hunyuan, Wan and many other local or custom-node backends
facts.dataFormat: Model weights under the local models directories, outputs on disk, and reproducible workflows as JSON or embedded PNG metadata
facts.gapVsPaid: You must choose and install models and design workflows yourself, and you lose Midjourney's unusually consistent house aesthetic and prompt simplicity.
facts.setupBlocker: Large model downloads and a compatible GPU; custom nodes add dependency, security and workflow complexity

alternatives.name: Draw Things
alternatives.desc: Excellent local generation on Apple hardware; the model choice is yours, so the taste is too.

facts.install: Install from the Apple App Store
facts.engines: Downloadable local diffusion models and adapters supported by Draw Things
facts.dataFormat: Models and generated images live in the app's local sandbox or selected local folder; core generation can run offline
facts.gapVsPaid: It has no single curated Midjourney-style model or aesthetic; output quality and taste depend on the models and settings you choose.
facts.setupBlocker: Apple hardware only, plus large model downloads and enough device memory

alternatives.name: Easy Diffusion
alternatives.desc: The easy local installer; output quality follows the model you download, not a secret Midjourney recipe.

facts.install: Download and run the one-click Windows installer, or unpack and run the Linux or macOS start script
facts.engines: Local diffusion checkpoints including Stable Diffusion, FLUX, Qwen, Z-Image and other supported architectures, with custom model files
facts.dataFormat: Model files and generated images are stored in the Easy Diffusion installation folders on the computer
facts.gapVsPaid: Its defaults and chosen open models are less consistently stylish than Midjourney, so strong results demand more model selection and prompting.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU or slow CPU fallback, at least roughly 25 GB of disk, model downloads, and possible Windows SmartScreen approval

alternatives.name: InvokeAI
alternatives.desc: A polished local studio for strong open image models; better editing, less instant house style.

facts.install: Install the Invoke launcher, then launch its local web application
facts.engines: Stable Diffusion 1.5, 2, XL and 3.5, FLUX, Qwen Image and supported API-backed image models
facts.dataFormat: Model weights, application database, gallery boards, images and generation metadata live on the local instance
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a better-controlled studio but requires model management and more decisions instead of Midjourney's fast, consistent house style.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU, launcher setup and large model downloads; API-backed models also need keys

alternatives.name: RuinedFooocus
alternatives.desc: The closest thing here to prompt-and-go; its defaults are friendly, its model stack less fashionable.

facts.install: Download the Windows archive and run run.bat, or install a Python virtual environment on Linux
facts.engines: SDXL and compatible local checkpoints, including newer FLUX, Krea and other supported model families, plus LoRAs and styles
facts.dataFormat: Models and outputs are stored in local application folders; generation settings can be embedded in image metadata
facts.gapVsPaid: Its defaults are approachable, but model quality and aesthetic consistency remain less predictable than Midjourney's curated service.
facts.setupBlocker: Large automatic model downloads and a capable GPU; Linux installation is source and virtual-environment based

alternatives.name: SwarmUI
alternatives.desc: A prompt-first local UI for current image models; you supply the model and GPU instead of renting the aesthetic.

facts.install: Run the Windows install batch file or Linux or macOS install script
facts.engines: ComfyUI-backed local models including Stable Diffusion, FLUX and newer image or video models, plus supported remote backends
facts.dataFormat: Models, configuration, generation history and output images live in the local SwarmUI installation
facts.gapVsPaid: It gives you control instead of a house model, so you supply the GPU, models and aesthetic judgment that Midjourney hides.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU and model downloads; the application is still labeled beta and first launch installs its backend

notes: Must-have no: one of the clearest frontier-model moat cases.
prompt:
Build me a local image-generation studio wrapping open models, in place of
Midjourney. Requirements:

- A local web app (Node + Express, plain HTML/JS) on localhost:4890: prompt box,
  a generate-4 button, and a gallery grid of results.
- Backend targets whichever engine I have: a local ComfyUI instance running Flux
  or SDXL if there is a GPU, otherwise a hosted API like Replicate or fal.ai
  (key in .env). Same UI either way.
- Save every image to ~/ImageGen/YYYY-MM/ with a sidecar JSON: prompt, seed,
  model, steps, so any result is reproducible later.
- Gallery search over past prompts via SQLite FTS5, favorites, and one-click
  re-run with the same seed or a new variation.
- Style presets in a styles.json of prompt prefixes and suffixes I can toggle,
  a poor man's style reference.
- No accounts, no telemetry, everything stays local except the hosted-API calls.
- Out of scope: training or fine-tuning models, and matching Midjourney's look.
  Build for reproducibility and control, not a taste layer.
- README: both engine setups, the rough cost per image on the hosted route, and
  a plain note that this is not Midjourney, the proprietary model and its years
  of aesthetic tuning cannot be rebuilt, this trades that for privacy and control.
